title: Burnt iron gets heavier
hook: Burning makes things vanish into flame. So why does burnt iron weigh more?

knows: that matter is made of atoms
doesNotKnow: that burning rearranges atoms rather than destroying them
that a burning metal can gain mass by taking oxygen from the air

misconception: Burning destroys matter, so the burnt thing always weighs less.
objective: The learner can explain that 10.0 g of iron burned completely to Fe2O3 weighs about 14.3 g, because the iron atoms stay and oxygen atoms from the air join them; mass is conserved when the air is counted too.

claims.text: 10.0 g of iron burned completely to iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3, gives about 14.3 g of ash.
claims.source: 10.0 g / 55.845 g/mol = 0.1791 mol Fe; Fe2O3 = 0.0895 mol x 159.687 g/mol = 14.30 g (node; Demo.tsx FINAL_G gives the same 14.30 g from 8 drawn Fe + 12 drawn O at the same scale). Molar masses: IUPAC 2021 standard atomic weights. · Fact-check 2026-10-13: Reproduced: FINAL_G = 14.297 g.

claims.text: Burning does not destroy atoms; it rearranges them, so the mass gained by the ash equals the mass of oxygen taken from the air.
claims.source: Law of conservation of mass (Lavoisier 1789; any general chemistry text, e.g. Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles, Fundamentals). Nuclear-scale mass changes from chemical energy are about 1e-10 of the mass, far below any scale.

claims.text: In Fe2O3, 2 iron atoms combine with 3 oxygen atoms.
claims.source: Formula of iron(III) oxide (haematite), CRC Handbook, 'Physical constants of inorganic compounds'.

claims.text: Wood seems to lose weight when it burns because its products, carbon dioxide and water vapour, escape into the air.
claims.source: Combustion of cellulose gives CO2 and H2O (Atkins & Jones, ch. on thermochemistry); ash is the small mineral residue.

claims.text: The stage is a toy: 8 drawn iron atoms stand for 10.0 g, and the lesson assumes all the iron becomes Fe2O3; real iron wool also forms some Fe3O4 and may not burn completely.
claims.source: Iron burning in air or oxygen gives mixtures of Fe3O4 and Fe2O3 (Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, ch. 25). Classroom steel-wool burns show a mass gain, typically smaller than 43% because burning is incomplete.

recall.question: Magnesium ribbon burns to white magnesium oxide powder. If you collect all the powder, compared with the ribbon it weighs…
recall.why: The magnesium atoms stay and oxygen atoms from the air join them, so the oxide weighs the metal plus the oxygen.
